prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro urban railway; Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC) primarily supervises train separation, movement authority and regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors, authorizes changes, directs recovery); Revenue Train Operator (sees movement authority limits, permitted speed, location confidence, radio condition, required actions on operator interface; acknowledgements reach Atlas via monitored path rejecting stale/inconsistent commands); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple; Cyber Security Officer (access control, security events, keys via Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, which supports onboard comms security material without changing safety logic). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (positions, regulation, alarms, commands; sends Crew Login Token Bundle at start of duty). North and South District Zone Controllers compute movement authority from location reports, occupancy and field state, send to Atlas. East and West Junction Interlockings: vital points/signals control; shall only accept commands satisfying safety rules; indications reach onboard via safety channels. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel (per train): active after operator authentication, energized and valid integrity; checks movement authority (sequence, applicability, consistency) before applying; speed enforcement, recalculates braking demand each cycle; door enable; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log after validating enforcement data set; states: initialization, protected manual, automatic train operation, fallback, cutout. Dual Channel Odometer: independent speed/distance; divergence beyond threshold degrades mode; reduced confidence increases position uncertainty and requests separation-preserving actions. Trainborne propulsion/brake interface converts safety commands, preserving isolation from non-vital circuits. Brake assurance verifies service/emergency brake via feedback, pressure, deceleration. Train Radio Modem: CBTC sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network; reports link quality, registration, session continuity to Atlas. Safety Data Communication Network: integrity, authentication, bounded latency; sends Clock Drift Sample Report at sync intervals. Service Timetable Server: schedule to Lantern (non-vital). Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital position/service data, cannot influence safety. Voice Dispatch Console: separate from vital path, degraded voice coordination. Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges door enable and closed-and-locked indications with train interface when berthed. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: collects non-vital trainborne health for Maple, no vital access. Modes: normal; degraded (safe state, reduced automation, human confirmation). Location/comms loss or vital disagreement shall restrict movement until resolved or degraded procedure approved.

New part:
S051: Wayside communications for Greenvale Metro are organized around continuous train radio coverage and a separated safety data backbone that carries vital movement authority traffic.
S052: The Wayside Radio Access Network is sometimes called Saffron in radio survey records, but this document uses Wayside Radio Access Network as the canonical name.
S053: The Wayside Radio Access Network provides overlapping cell coverage through stations, tunnels, crossovers, and depot approach tracks so that the Train Radio Modem can maintain a stable session during normal operation.
S054: Radio sites are engineered with sector overlap at station throats and interlocking approaches because these locations combine frequent braking, switching, and train-to-wayside message activity.
S055: The Train Radio Modem maintains the active bearer used by the Atlas Onboard Controller and reports radio quality changes before the session reaches the minimum design margin.
S056: Handover is planned as a make-before-break event where practical, with the old radio path retained until the new path has accepted the session and passed basic message checks.
S057: If radio quality degrades faster than predicted, the onboard equipment falls back to the last validated movement authority rules rather than accepting unverified wayside data.
S058: The Safety Data Communication Network carries vital messages between zone controllers, interlockings, and approved interfaces using deterministic routing and monitored latency limits.
S059: The Safety Data Communication Network is physically and logically separated from maintenance and passenger information traffic to reduce exposure to congestion and non-vital configuration changes.
S060: Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the authentication framework used on the safety data paths and is managed under controlled access by authorized technical staff.
S061: North District Zone Controller is sometimes called Marble in legacy boundary diagrams, but this document uses North District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S062: South District Zone Controller is sometimes called Orchid in commissioning notes, but this document uses South District Zone Controller as the canonical name.
S063: North District Zone Controller supervises the northern main line, the northern turnback, and the approach to East Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S064: South District Zone Controller supervises the southern main line, the southern turnback, and the approach to West Junction Interlocking within its configured limits.
S065: The boundary between North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is defined by track section ownership, radio coverage overlap, and the point at which a train authority must be reissued by the receiving zone.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
